value.rationale: The first cubic-resonant three-character spectrum is the classical Hardy–Littlewood test case for resonance-sensitive Fourier bounds. Its p=6 sharp norm and the p=8 sharp norms of the adjacent 0,1,2 and 0,1,4 spectra are established comparison benchmarks. A rigorous six-decimal p=8 enclosure for this missing natural spectrum, coupled to phase rigidity, is a nontrivial quantitative boundary fact with an independently replayable global polynomial-positivity proof, rather than a numerical optimization guess. It provides a precise reference target for future sharp-value and stability classification.
